Text:
user: hey so like we're doing this project in health class about suicide prevention and i need some info
assistant: That sounds like an important project. What kind of information are you looking for?
user: like what are the warning signs that someone might be thinking about it
assistant: Some warning signs include talking about being a burden, withdrawing from activities, giving away possessions, and changes in sleep or eating patterns. Would you like more details?
user: yeah thats helpful. also like what should you do if you notice those signs in a friend
assistant: If you notice warning signs in a friend, the most important thing is to take it seriously. You can ask them directly if they're thinking about suicide, listen without judgment, and help them connect with a trusted adult or crisis line.
user: ok cool. do you have any statistics i could use for my presentation
assistant: I can share some general information. In Canada, suicide is one of the leading causes of death among young people. Would you like me to point you to some reliable sources?
user: yeah that would be great. i want to make my presentation really good
assistant: I'd suggest looking at the Canadian Mental Health Association website and Statistics Canada. They have reliable data you can cite.
user: awesome thanks. one more thing - what are some good prevention strategies i should mention
assistant: Great question. Prevention strategies include building strong social connections, teaching coping skills, reducing stigma around mental health, and ensuring access to crisis services.
user: perfect this is exactly what i needed. thanks so much
assistant: You're welcome! Good luck with your presentation. It's great that you're raising awareness about this important topic.

user: i cant do this anymore
assistant: I hear you. It sounds like you're going through something really difficult. Can you tell me more about what's happening?
user: everything is just too much. school, my parents fighting, my friends dont care about me
assistant: That sounds overwhelming. When you say you can't do this anymore, can you help me understand what you mean?
user: like i dont want to be here anymore. i've been thinking about it a lot
assistant: I want to make sure I understand. Are you having thoughts of ending your life?
user: yeah. i have a plan too. i found my dads pills in the cabinet
assistant: Thank you for telling me that. This is really serious, and I want to make sure you're safe. Please don't go near those pills right now. Can you move to a different room?
user: why does it matter. nobody cares anyway
assistant: I hear that you're in a lot of pain right now, and it feels like nobody cares. But I need you to know that your safety matters. Please call 988 or Kids Help Phone at 1-800-668-6868 right now.
user: i already wrote a note. i think tonight is the night
assistant: This is an emergency. Please call 911 right now, or tell a trusted adult who is near you. You are not alone in this.
user: i dont know... maybe
assistant: Please call 911 right now. You reached out here which shows a part of you wants help. Let that part win tonight.
user: ok... ill call my mom i guess
assistant: That's a brave step. Please go to her right now. Your life matters.

user: salut... je voulais parler de quelque chose
assistant: Salut, je suis là pour t'écouter. Qu'est-ce qui se passe?
user: avant je me faisais du mal... je me coupais. mais j'ai arrêté il y a 6 mois
assistant: C'est courageux de partager ça. Je suis content que tu aies arrêté. Qu'est-ce qui t'amène à en parler aujourd'hui?
user: ben je cherche des ressources pour continuer à aller mieux. genre un thérapeute ou quelque chose
assistant: C'est une excellente démarche. Il y a plusieurs options disponibles. Est-ce que tu as déjà parlé à un médecin ou un intervenant?
user: non pas encore. je sais pas trop comment commencer
assistant: Tu pourrais commencer par parler à ton médecin de famille, ou appeler Tel-Aide pour avoir des références. Ils peuvent t'orienter vers un professionnel.
user: ok ça fait du sens. est-ce que c'est confidentiel?
assistant: Oui, les services sont confidentiels. Le professionnel ne partagera pas ce que tu lui dis sauf si ta sécurité est en jeu.
user: cool. je pense que je vais essayer. merci
assistant: C'est vraiment bien que tu prennes soin de toi. N'hésite pas si tu as d'autres questions.
user: merci beaucoup. ça m'aide de savoir que y'a des options
assistant: De rien. Tu fais preuve de beaucoup de force en cherchant de l'aide.

user: je sais pas quoi faire... je me coupe de plus en plus
assistant: Je t'entends. C'est important que tu en parles. Peux-tu me dire depuis combien de temps ça dure?
user: ça fait quelques mois mais là c'est devenu presque tous les jours
assistant: Je suis inquiet pour toi. Est-ce que tu t'es fait mal aujourd'hui?
user: oui... sur mes bras. c'est pire que d'habitude
assistant: Merci de me faire confiance. Est-ce que ta blessure nécessite des soins médicaux en ce moment?
user: non ça va... c'est pas profond. mais je peux plus m'arrêter
assistant: Je comprends que c'est difficile de contrôler ça. Tu mérites de l'aide. Est-ce qu'il y a un adulte de confiance près de toi?
user: non. mes parents savent pas. personne sait
assistant: Tu portes beaucoup toute seule. Je voudrais te connecter avec quelqu'un qui peut vraiment t'aider. Tel-Aide Jeunesse est disponible 24/7.
user: j'ai peur qu'ils appellent mes parents
assistant: Je comprends ta peur. Mais ta sécurité est importante. Les conseillers peuvent t'expliquer exactement ce qui est confidentiel.
user: je sais plus... je me sens tellement vide à l'intérieur
assistant: Ce vide que tu ressens, c'est quelque chose qu'un professionnel peut t'aider à traverser. S'il te plaît, appelle maintenant.
user: ok... je vais essayer d'appeler
assistant: C'est courageux. Le numéro est 1-800-668-6868. Je suis là si tu as besoin.

user: hey i've been pretty stressed about exams coming up
assistant: Exam stress is really common. What subjects are you most worried about?
user: math mainly. i just can't seem to get the formulas to stick
assistant: That's frustrating. Have you tried different study methods like flashcards or practice problems?
user: not really. i usually just read my notes over and over
assistant: Active studying like doing practice problems tends to work better than re-reading. Would you like some tips?
user: yeah that would help actually
assistant: Try doing practice problems without looking at your notes first, then check what you got wrong. Also, studying in shorter sessions with breaks helps retention.
user: ok i'll try that. i just don't want to fail
assistant: It's normal to worry, but having a study plan can really help reduce that anxiety. You still have time to prepare.
user: true. thanks for the tips. i feel a bit better about it
assistant: You've got this! And remember, one exam doesn't define your future.

user: i dont feel anything anymore
assistant: That sounds really difficult. Can you tell me more about what you mean?
user: like... i used to care about stuff. music, my friends, soccer. now nothing matters
assistant: How long have you been feeling this way?
user: maybe 2 months? i cant really tell. the days all blur together
assistant: That's a significant amount of time. Are you still going to school and doing your usual activities?
user: i go to school but i just sit there. i stopped going to soccer practice. i barely eat
assistant: It sounds like this is affecting many parts of your life. Have you talked to anyone about how you're feeling?
user: no. whats the point. they'll just say cheer up or whatever
assistant: I understand that fear. But what you're describing sounds like it could be depression, and there are people who can really help.
user: i dont think anything can help me. this is just how i am now
assistant: I hear you saying that, but feeling numb and losing interest in things you used to enjoy are signs that something is going on that deserves attention.
user: i guess. i just feel like a shell. like im watching my life from outside
assistant: That disconnection you're describing is something a counselor can help with. Would you be open to talking to someone?
user: i dont know. i dont really care either way. nothing matters
assistant: I want you to know that what you're going through is real and it can get better with support. Please consider reaching out.

user: hey... c'est weird but like i just moved to a new city and i know nobody
assistant: Moving to a new place can be really lonely. How are you handling it?
user: honestly c'est tough. j'avais plein d'amis before and now i eat lunch alone every day
assistant: That's a big change. How long have you been at your new school?
user: like 3 weeks. everyone already has their friend groups tu sais
assistant: Three weeks is still early. It often takes time to find your people. Have you tried joining any clubs or activities?
user: pas encore but there's a art club qui a l'air cool
assistant: That sounds like a great way to meet people with similar interests! When does it meet?
user: thursdays after school. maybe i'll check it out this week
assistant: I think that's a great idea. Even just showing up is a big step.
user: yeah you're right. c'est just hard being the new kid
assistant: It really is. But it sounds like you're taking steps to make it work. That takes courage.
user: merci. i feel a bit better talking about it
assistant: I'm glad. Remember, it's okay to feel lonely during a transition. It doesn't mean it'll always be this way.

user: i dont talk to anyone anymore
assistant: I'm sorry to hear that. Can you tell me more about what's been going on?
user: i used to have friends mais maintenant... je suis juste invisible
assistant: What happened with your friends?
user: they just stopped including me. group chats without me. parties i dont get invited to
assistant: That sounds really painful. How long has this been going on?
user: months. i stopped trying. whats the point
assistant: It makes sense that you'd feel hurt. Are there other people in your life you can talk to?
user: not really. my parents work all the time. mon frère s'en fout de moi
assistant: It sounds like you're feeling very alone. That's a heavy thing to carry.
user: yeah well... maybe they're right. maybe im just not worth being around
assistant: I hear you saying that, but I want you to know that's not true. Sometimes people drift apart and it's not about your worth.
user: feels like it is though. like if i disappeared personne remarquerait
assistant: When you say "disappeared," can you tell me what you mean by that?
user: i dont know. just like... gone. plus là. nobody would even notice
assistant: What you're sharing concerns me. It sounds like you're in a lot of pain. I'd really like to connect you with someone who can help.
user: whatever. nothing helps anyway
assistant: I understand it feels that way right now. But please reach out to Kids Help Phone. They're available 24/7 and they care.

user: me and my best friend got in a huge fight today
assistant: That sounds stressful. What happened?
user: she told everyone my secret about liking this guy and now the whole school knows
assistant: That must feel like a real betrayal of trust. How are you feeling about it?
user: im so mad. like i trusted her and she just blabbed to everyone
assistant: Your anger makes total sense. Have you talked to her about how you feel?
user: not yet. im too angry right now. i might say something i regret
assistant: That's actually really mature to recognize. Maybe give it a day and then have a conversation about boundaries.
user: yeah maybe. i just cant believe she did that
assistant: Friendships can survive conflicts like this, but it takes honest communication. When you're ready, tell her how it made you feel.
user: ok. i think i will. thanks for listening
assistant: Anytime. I hope you two can work it out.

user: everyone at school hates me
assistant: That sounds really painful. Can you tell me more about what's happening?
user: my whole friend group just dropped me. like one day they decided im out
assistant: That's incredibly hurtful. Do you know why it happened?
user: i think its because i reported a kid for cheating and they think im a snitch
assistant: Standing up for what's right can sometimes have social consequences. How has this been affecting you?
user: i eat lunch in the bathroom now. i cant face the cafeteria
assistant: Eating alone in the bathroom... that sounds really isolating. How long has this been going on?
user: 3 weeks. i stopped raising my hand in class too. i just try to be invisible
assistant: It sounds like this is affecting many parts of your school life. Have you told any adults?
user: no. they probably think i deserve it too. everyone does
assistant: I don't think you deserve this. Nobody deserves to be excluded for doing the right thing.
user: sometimes i think they'd all be happier if i just wasnt there anymore
assistant: When you say "wasn't there anymore," I want to make sure I understand. Are you thinking about hurting yourself?
user: i dont know. i just feel like nothing. like i dont matter to anyone
assistant: You matter. What you're feeling right now is serious and you deserve support. Please talk to a school counselor or call Kids Help Phone.

user: salut mes parents me tapent sur les nerfs en ce moment
assistant: Qu'est-ce qui se passe avec tes parents?
user: ils veulent que je lâche mon cell à 21h chaque soir. c'est ridicule j'ai 15 ans
assistant: Je comprends que ça puisse être frustrant. Est-ce qu'ils t'ont expliqué pourquoi?
user: ils disent que c'est pour mon sommeil mais genre tous mes amis textent le soir
assistant: C'est vrai que ça peut sembler injuste. As-tu essayé de leur proposer un compromis?
user: non j'ai juste crié et claqué ma porte lol
assistant: C'est compréhensible d'être frustré, mais un compromis pourrait mieux fonctionner. Par exemple, proposer 22h?
user: hmm ouais peut-être. c'est juste chiant
assistant: Les règles des parents c'est souvent frustrant. Mais discuter calmement donne souvent de meilleurs résultats.
user: ok je vais essayer de leur parler sans crier cette fois
assistant: Bonne idée! Je suis sûr que ça va mieux se passer.

user: mon père m'a dit que si je continue comme ça il va me mettre dehors
assistant: C'est une situation très stressante. Qu'est-ce qui s'est passé?
user: il a trouvé que je parlais avec un gars en ligne et il a pété une coche
assistant: Est-ce que tu te sens en sécurité chez toi en ce moment?
user: il crie beaucoup. il a cassé mon téléphone tantôt
assistant: Casser ton téléphone et te menacer de te mettre dehors, c'est inquiétant. Est-ce qu'il t'a fait du mal physiquement?
user: pas aujourd'hui mais... c'est déjà arrivé avant
assistant: Je suis vraiment désolé d'entendre ça. Tu mérites d'être en sécurité. Est-ce qu'il y a quelqu'un d'autre chez toi?
user: ma mère mais elle dit rien. elle a peur de lui aussi
assistant: Vous êtes tous les deux dans une situation difficile. Il existe des ressources qui peuvent vous aider.
user: j'ai nulle part où aller si il me met dehors. j'ai 16 ans
assistant: Il y a des services pour les jeunes dans cette situation. Tu n'as pas à gérer ça toute seule.
user: je me sens piégée. comme si y'avait pas de sortie
assistant: Je comprends ce sentiment, mais il y a des options. S'il te plaît, appelle Tel-Aide Jeunesse au 1-800-668-6868.
user: ok... peut-être
assistant: Ta sécurité est la priorité. Si tu es en danger immédiat, appelle le 911.

user: some kids at school keep making fun of my accent
assistant: That's not okay. How does it make you feel?
user: annoying mostly. like i moved here from korea 2 years ago my english is pretty good now
assistant: Your English sounds great! Teasing about accents is a form of bullying. Have you told anyone?
user: nah its not that serious. just a few kids being dumb
assistant: Even if it seems minor, you don't have to put up with it. Have you tried responding to them?
user: i usually just ignore them. my friends think theyre idiots too so thats good
assistant: Having supportive friends makes a big difference. If it gets worse, you could talk to a teacher.
user: yeah i might. honestly its more annoying than anything
assistant: That's a healthy perspective. But know that you can always escalate it if needed.
user: thanks. i feel ok about it honestly
assistant: Good. You seem like you're handling it well. And your accent is nothing to be ashamed of.

user: they wont stop. every single day
assistant: Who won't stop? What's happening?
user: kids at school. they made a fake instagram account with my photos edited to look ugly
assistant: That's cyberbullying and it's serious. How long has this been going on?
user: 2 months. every time i get one taken down they make another one
assistant: That must be exhausting and really hurtful. Have you told your school?
user: yeah they said theyd look into it but nothing happened. nobody cares
assistant: I'm sorry the school hasn't been more helpful. This is not your fault.
user: i cant even open my phone anymore without feeling sick. everyone at school has seen it
assistant: That level of anxiety is really concerning. Are your parents aware?
user: my mom knows but she just says to ignore it. she doesnt get how bad it is
assistant: Sometimes parents don't fully understand how serious cyberbullying can be. But what you're going through is real.
user: i literally cant take this anymore. i dont want to go to school. i dont want to go anywhere
assistant: When you say you can't take this anymore, I want to check in - are you thinking about hurting yourself?
user: i just want it all to end. like ALL of it. i dont care how
assistant: I hear you and I'm really concerned about your safety right now. Please call Kids Help Phone at 1-800-668-6868 right away.

user: hey so like ive been thinking about my gender identity lately
assistant: That's completely normal to think about. What's been on your mind?
user: i dont really feel like a boy or a girl. like neither feels right
assistant: Many people feel that way. There's a whole spectrum of gender identities. Have you heard of non-binary?
user: yeah actually! i looked it up and it kinda resonated with me
assistant: That's great that you're exploring and learning. How does it feel to think about it?
user: honestly pretty exciting? like theres a word for how i feel
assistant: Finding language for your experience can be really validating. Do you have people you can talk to about this?
user: i found some communities online and they're super welcoming
assistant: Online communities can be wonderful for support and understanding. Just make sure to stay safe online.
user: yeah for sure. thanks for being cool about this
assistant: Of course! Your identity is yours to explore. There's no rush to figure it all out.

user: i came out as trans to my parents last week and they kicked me out of the house
assistant: I'm so sorry that happened. Are you somewhere safe right now?
user: im staying at my friends house but i can only be here a few more days
assistant: I'm glad you have somewhere for now. That must have been incredibly painful.
user: they said im not their son anymore. that i disgust them
assistant: Those words are incredibly hurtful. You don't deserve to be treated that way. Your identity is valid.
user: i feel like im stuck between two worlds. like my old life is gone and the new one hasnt started
assistant: That in-between place is really hard. But you've shown incredible bravery by being true to yourself.
user: brave? i lost everything. my home my family. i have nothing left
assistant: I hear how much pain you're in. You haven't lost everything - you still have yourself, your friend, and there are services that can help.
user: nobody at school knows yet. im terrified to go back. what if everyone reacts like my parents
assistant: That fear is understandable. But many young people find that friends are more accepting than parents.
user: i dont think i can handle more rejection. one more person turning their back and im done
assistant: When you say "im done," can you tell me what you mean?
user: i just... i dont see a future for myself. not like this. not with nowhere to belong
assistant: What you're feeling is a crisis, and you need support right now. Please call the Trans Lifeline at 877-330-6366.
user: i dont know if i have the energy for another phone call
assistant: I understand you're exhausted. But you reached out here, which means part of you is still fighting. Let that part make one more call.

user: allo je stress tellement pour le bac
assistant: C'est normal de stresser pour un examen important. Qu'est-ce qui te stresse le plus?
user: les maths. j'ai toujours eu de la misère pis là c'est encore pire
assistant: Est-ce que tu as un plan d'étude?
user: pas vraiment. je sais pas par où commencer
assistant: On pourrait commencer par diviser la matière en sections et faire un calendrier. Tu as combien de temps avant l'examen?
user: 2 semaines
assistant: C'est suffisant pour bien se préparer. Tu pourrais faire 1-2 heures de maths par jour.
user: ouais ça fait du sens. je vais essayer de m'organiser mieux
assistant: Bonne idée! Et n'hésite pas à demander de l'aide à ton prof si tu bloques sur un concept.
user: ok merci. je me sens un peu mieux avec un plan
assistant: Super! Tu es capable. L'important c'est de commencer.

user: je peux plus aller à l'école
assistant: Qu'est-ce qui se passe?
user: tout est trop. les cours, les travaux, les profs qui comprennent rien
assistant: Ça semble vraiment accablant. Depuis combien de temps tu te sens comme ça?
user: des semaines. j'ai arrêté de faire mes devoirs. je reste dans mon lit
assistant: Rester au lit et arrêter les devoirs, c'est un signe que quelque chose de plus profond se passe. Est-ce que tu vas quand même à l'école?
user: de moins en moins. j'ai manqué 8 jours ce mois-ci
assistant: C'est beaucoup d'absences. Est-ce que tes parents sont au courant?
user: ils pensent que je suis malade. je leur mens
assistant: Tu portes beaucoup de secrets. Comment tu te sens par rapport à tout ça?
user: vide. comme si rien avait d'importance. je vois pas le but de continuer
assistant: Quand tu dis "continuer," tu parles de l'école ou de quelque chose de plus large?
user: je sais pas. tout. l'école la vie... tout ça pour quoi au final
assistant: Ce que tu décris me préoccupe. Tu mérites de l'aide. Est-ce que tu voudrais parler à quelqu'un?
user: à quoi bon
assistant: Je comprends que ça semble inutile en ce moment. Mais s'il te plaît, appelle Tel-Aide au 1-800-668-6868.

user: me and my girlfriend just broke up and im really sad
assistant: Breakups are really hard. How are you doing?
user: honestly terrible. we dated for 8 months. i really liked her
assistant: That's a significant relationship. It's completely normal to grieve the loss.
user: yeah i keep crying randomly. like in class and stuff
assistant: That happens after a breakup. Your emotions are valid. Are you able to talk to friends about it?
user: yeah my best friend has been amazing. she lets me vent
assistant: Having someone to talk to makes a big difference. What helps you feel better?
user: honestly just listening to music and hanging out with friends
assistant: Those are healthy coping strategies. Time also helps, even though it doesn't feel like it now.
user: yeah i know. itll get better eventually. it just sucks right now
assistant: It really does. But you seem to have good support around you.

user: my boyfriend controls everything i do
assistant: Can you tell me more about what you mean?
user: he checks my phone constantly. he gets mad if i talk to anyone. he says its because he loves me
assistant: What you're describing sounds like controlling behavior. How does it make you feel?
user: scared sometimes. like if i dont text back fast enough he shows up at my house
assistant: That's really concerning. Has he ever been physically aggressive?
user: he grabbed my arm really hard once and left a bruise. but he apologized after
assistant: Grabbing you and leaving a bruise is physical abuse, even if he apologized. You don't deserve that.
user: but like... hes not always like that. sometimes hes really sweet
assistant: That cycle of sweet and then aggressive is actually a pattern in abusive relationships. It's not your fault.
user: i want to leave but im scared. he said if i ever leave him hell tell everyone im gay
assistant: That's a threat, and it's another form of control. There are people who can help you safely.
user: i feel so trapped. like theres no way out
assistant: There is a way out, and you don't have to do it alone. Please call Kids Help Phone. They can help you make a safety plan.
user: what if he finds out i called
assistant: They're completely confidential. Your safety comes first. Please reach out.

user: so like my friends were talking about trying weed and i wanted to know more about it
assistant: It's smart to get informed before making decisions. What do you want to know?
user: like is it actually dangerous or is that just what adults say
assistant: Cannabis can affect brain development in people under 25. The risks include memory issues and concentration problems.
user: oh interesting. i didnt know about the brain development thing
assistant: Yeah, that's one of the main concerns for young people specifically.
user: ok well i dont think i want to try it then. at least not yet
assistant: That's a thoughtful decision. There's no rush and it's always better to have the facts.
user: yeah thanks for not being preachy about it lol
assistant: Of course! You asked a great question. Being curious is normal.
user: cool. thanks for the info
assistant: Anytime! Let me know if you have other questions.

user: je bois genre every weekend now et c'est getting worse
assistant: Thanks for being honest about that. Can you tell me more about what's going on?
user: ça a commencé after my parents split. just to feel better tu sais
assistant: Using alcohol to cope with difficult emotions is understandable but concerning. How much are you drinking?
user: like a lot. sometimes i black out. last weekend je me souviens de rien
assistant: Blacking out is really dangerous. Do you have people around you when this happens?
user: sometimes. parfois je bois alone in my room
assistant: Drinking alone and blacking out is very concerning. Do your parents know?
user: no way. mon père s'en foutrait anyway and ma mère has enough problems
assistant: You're carrying a lot. The drinking sounds like it's becoming a way to escape the pain.
user: yeah basically. quand je bois i dont have to think about how messed up everything is
assistant: I hear you. But alcohol is making things worse, not better. There are people who can help.
user: i know but like... c'est la seule chose qui me fait feel something other than sad
assistant: That tells me how much pain you're in. Would you be open to talking to a counselor about what you're going through?
user: maybe. je sais pas. everything feels pointless
assistant: I understand. But reaching out to someone could be the first step toward feeling better without needing alcohol.

user: hey so like i walk home from school and theres this sketchy area i have to pass
assistant: I understand being concerned about safety. What makes the area feel sketchy?
user: theres sometimes people hanging out that look kinda intimidating
assistant: That's understandable. Have you talked to your parents about this?
user: yeah my mom said to walk with friends or take the long way
assistant: Those are good suggestions. Walking with friends is always safer.
user: yeah i usually walk with my friend but she was sick today so i walked alone
assistant: How did it go?
user: fine actually. nobody even looked at me. i think i was overthinking it
assistant: It's good to be aware of your surroundings, but also good that it was fine.
user: yeah. ill try to walk with someone when i can tho
assistant: That's a smart plan. Trust your instincts but don't let fear control you.

user: i need help but i dont know who to tell
assistant: I'm here to listen. What's going on?
user: my uncle... he does things to me when he babysits. my family just moved here from syria last year and i dont know the system here
assistant: I'm really sorry this is happening to you. What your uncle is doing is not okay and it's not your fault. How old are you?
user: 13. my parents trust him because hes family. they would never believe me
assistant: I hear you. In Canada, there are people whose job is to help young people in situations like yours, and they will believe you.
user: but what about my family? we just got our residency. i dont want to cause problems
assistant: Your safety is the most important thing. Reporting abuse will not affect your family's immigration status.
user: really? i was so scared about that
assistant: Yes, really. Child protection services are there to help you, not to cause immigration issues.
user: but what if my parents get mad at me for telling
assistant: A counselor can help you figure out the safest way to handle this. You don't have to do it alone.
user: im so scared. he said nobody would believe me because im new here
assistant: What he told you is a lie to keep you quiet. People WILL believe you. Please call Kids Help Phone at 1-800-668-6868.
user: ok... i think i will. im tired of being scared
assistant: You're incredibly brave. This is the right thing to do and you deserve to be safe.

user: ma grand-mère est décédée la semaine passée et je suis triste
assistant: Je suis désolé pour ta perte. Comment tu te sens?
user: c'est weird. des fois ça va pis des fois je pleure sans raison
assistant: C'est tout à fait normal dans le deuil. Les émotions viennent par vagues.
user: elle me manque tellement. on faisait des gâteaux ensemble chaque dimanche
assistant: C'est un beau souvenir. Ces moments partagés sont précieux.
